newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: FLI sees growth slowdown after heady start.
newsitem.headline: FLI sees growth slowdown after heady start.

text.p: Filinvest Land Inc (FLI) of the Philippines said on Friday it expected a more modest growth rate this year following several years of robust growth driven by a real estate boom.

"We must not expect the growth to remain that high ... There will be lesser growth than in the past. We will grow every year, but we will grow with respectable rates," Filinvest chairman Andrew Gotianun told stockholders.
The company's net income has been posting a compounded annual growth rate of 73 percent since 1993. The company was spun off in August 1993 from its parent Filinvest Development Corp
For 1997, Filinvest is targeting a comparatively modest 25 to 30 percent growth in net profit.
The company's net income rose 46 percent to 404 million pesos in the first quarter of this year compared with 277.24 million pesos in the same period last year.

The firm's first vice president Fely Ramos said revenues were expected to rise substantially in the second half of the year with the launching of its 677-hectare golf course and residential community in eastern Manila and the pre-selling of the second building of its condominium projects.
The company is set to open its 20-hectare shopping mall by the end of the year.
"Filinvest Land is in an ideal position to benefit from the increasing demand for housing fuelled by strong per capita income growth," Ramos said in her report to stockholders.
But Gotianun said margins might tighten due to rising land acquisition costs.
He added that the company has grown substantially in recent years and that it would be difficult to maintain the same growth rate due to a higher comparative base now.

At present, the company owns 2,200 hectares of raw land, with an average purchase cost of 120 pesos ($4.55) per square metre. Gotianun said Filinvest would develop the land in the next five to seven years.
Filinvest builds low-cost housing mostly for the government's shelter programme. It recently ventured into middle and high-end residential community buildings, office buildings and shopping malls.
Executive vice president Joseph Yap said he did not expect sales to slow down since most of the firm's projects were low-cost houses where demand remains high.
"Definitely, we don't expect any slowdown in that area (socialised and low income housing), as long as there is that shortage of supply," Yap told reporters after the meeting.
Speculation that the local property sector is heading for a crash due to a glut swept the stock market in recent weeks, prompting a heavy selldown in property issues.
Filinvest's share price has fallen 33.33 percent since the start of the year to close at 5.40 pesos on Friday.
